meaning: The number 150 is best known as the total number of psalms in the Book of Psalms, symbolizing the completeness of praise and prayer to God.
description: In biblical tradition, 150 is first and foremost linked to the 150 psalms in Tehillim (the Book of Psalms), which cover the full spectrum of human experience in relation to God—from lament and repentance to praise and worship. The number 150 is also central to the flood narrative: the waters stood over the earth for 150 days (Genesis 7:24), and it was after 150 days that the waters began to recede (Genesis 8:3). In this way, this number marks both God's judgment and the turning point toward restoration. In Jewish tradition, the 150 psalms play a central role in liturgy and daily prayer, and the number thus represents a wholeness of spiritual expression.

footnotes.text: In rabbinic tradition, the Book of Psalms is divided into five books (Psalms 1–41, 42–72, 73–89, 90–106, 107–150), mirroring the five Books of Moses (Chumash). This division emphasizes that praise holds a central place alongside the Torah in Jewish devotional life.

Psalm 150, the final psalm, serves as a grand concluding doxology where everything that has breath is called to praise the Lord. In synagogue liturgy, this psalm is part of Pesukei de-Zimra (verses of praise), recited daily in the morning prayer.

The number 150 also appears in other biblical contexts: Nehemiah had 150 Jews and officials at his table daily (Nehemiah 5:17), illustrating his hospitality and leadership, and Ulam had 150 descendants who were skilled warriors (1 Chronicles 8:40).
